questions.prompt: Week 17 · The Great Depression and the Crisis of Confidence: What is the strongest method for evaluating “Explaining Economic Collapse”?
choices: Accept the source because it was created during the period.
Reject the source if it has a perspective or purpose.
Compare it with independent evidence and evaluate origin, purpose, context, value, and limits.
Use only the most memorable statement.
questions.explanation: Historical evidence is evaluated through sourcing, contextualization, corroboration, and attention to limitations.
questions.skill: Unit 4 · The United States and the World · Week 17

questions.prompt: A time series plots unemployment, bank failures, industrial output, and prices from 1929 onward. What is the safest inference?
choices: The measures document a severe, interconnected contraction, but movement together does not prove that one series alone caused the others.
The first series to rise caused every later change.
Unemployment data make banking evidence unnecessary.
A national time series proves every community experienced the crisis identically.
questions.explanation: Time-series co-movement can reveal an interconnected crisis but does not by itself establish one-way causation or uniform local experience.
